name: Tabs
description: A set of layered sections (tab panels) that display one panel at a time, with tab elements that activate corresponding panels.

keyboard_interactions.action: Moves focus into tab list on active tab; next Tab exits to tab panel
Moves focus to previous tab (horizontal); wraps from first to last
Moves focus to next tab (horizontal); wraps from last to first
Moves focus to previous tab (vertical); wraps
Moves focus to next tab (vertical); wraps
Activates focused tab if not auto-activated on focus
(Optional) Closes the current tab and panel if deletable

required_attributes.description: State. Exactly one tab is true. Does NOT control focus — pair it with roving tabindex.
Roving tabindex: 0 on the selected tab, -1 on all others. Not an ARIA attribute, but non-optional for this pattern — without it every tab is a Tab stop.

optional_attributes.description: menu or true if the tab has a popup

notes: Only one tab panel should be visible at a time
Roving tabindex is mandatory in practice: tabindex='0' on the selected tab, '-1' on the rest. The tablist is ONE Tab stop; arrows move between tabs.
Automatic activation (selection follows focus) is fine when panels are cheap to render. Use manual activation (arrows move, Enter/Space selects) when switching is expensive or destructive.
Moving focus with arrows means calling .focus() yourself — aria-selected does not move focus.
If a panel contains no focusable element, give the panel tabindex='0' so keyboard users can reach and scroll its content.
Hide inactive panels with the `hidden` attribute — not opacity, z-index stacking, or off-screen positioning (RAWeb 10.8).
Style the focus ring separately from the selected state: they are different things and can be on different tabs during manual activation.
native_element: none — tabs have no native HTML element; ARIA is mandatory here

raweb_criteria.reason: tab/tablist/tabpanel roles and aria-selected must be exposed, since no native element conveys them.
Arrow keys must move between tabs and the widget must be fully operable by keyboard and pointer.
The focused tab must show a visible indicator, distinct from the selected tab's styling.
Inactive panels must be hidden from assistive technologies, not just visually stacked behind the active one.
Roving tabindex must keep the navigation sequence coherent: one Tab stop for the whole tablist, landing on the selected tab.
Roving tabindex is the classic keyboard-trap risk — Tab must always exit the tablist to the panel.
